subdomain: 2.4 Optimize context windows and manage token usage

en.question: An investigation assistant loads every diagnostic file before each analysis, although most tasks inspect only a few files. Irrelevant material reduces retrieval focus within the prompt. A read tool can fetch exact file sections from durable storage, and a small amount of extra tool latency is acceptable. Which context strategy best matches these constraints?

options.text: Keep loading all files and move the instructions to the end so irrelevant content no longer consumes context.
options.note: Prompt order can affect attention but does not remove irrelevant tokens. It leaves the full-corpus loading cost and context occupancy unchanged.

options.text: Keep file references and metadata in context; fetch exact sections when the investigation needs them.
options.note: Just-in-time retrieval defers detailed content until it is relevant. Durable references preserve access to exact evidence while accepting some runtime retrieval latency.

options.text: Replace the files with one short permanent summary and remove the read tool to eliminate retrieval overhead.
options.note: A fixed summary can omit details required by a later investigation. Removing the read tool also removes the stated route back to exact source evidence.

options.text: Cache the unchanged full file collection and keep sending the same complete context on every request.
options.note: Caching can reduce repeated processing but does not remove irrelevant material from the model's context. It does not address the observed loss of focus.

references.title: Effective context engineering for AI agents
